# HowMaHiCo

A parameterized RMarkdown reporting workflow for
**LC-immunopeptidomics** (MHC/HLA peptide) data analysis. It ingests
LC-MS search-engine output from multiple tools (FragPipe, DIA-NN,
PEAKS), normalizes it into a single unified long-format table
(`pep_all`), and renders self-contained, interactive HTML QC reports
plus csv/xlsx result exports.

**Distributed as an R package.**
[`library(HowMaHiCo)`](https://github.com/DavidGZ1/HowMaHiCo) gives you
the full function library and all nine report templates. See
`project-style-guide.md` for the longer-term R-package + Docker + Shiny
distribution pattern.

## Quickstart

``` r

remotes::install_github("DavidGZ1/HowMaHiCo")

HowMaHiCo::get_pipeline_script("howmahico_pipeline.R")
```

Open that script and source it. It starts in demo mode, so it runs the
whole pipeline against a small simulated dataset shipped with the
package — no data of your own required. Then set `RUN_DEMO <- FALSE`,
edit the `CONFIG` block at the top, and re-run.
[`vignette("howmahico")`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/articles/howmahico.md)
narrates the same walkthrough.

## What it does

    LC-MS search output (FragPipe psm.tsv, DIA-NN report.tsv, PEAKS peptide.csv)
          │   read + parse + annotate  (software-specific loaders converge on one schema)
          ▼
    pep_all  — unified long-format peptide table
          │
          ▼
    inst/rmarkdown/templates/00_mhc_report/skeleton/skeleton.Rmd
          │   rendered via run_howmahico_report() — self-contained interactive HTML
          │   (ID counts, replicate/condition overlaps, size & charge distributions,
          │    RT/ion-mobility/m_z "pseudochromatograms", Area correlation & %CV,
          │    Score/ppm QC, sequence motifs, PTM profile)
          ▼
    csv / xlsx result tables  +  optional PNG figure exports

Each report is rendered once per analysis subset (e.g. acquisition mode
× sample group), driven by an annotation CSV that maps raw data files to
experimental conditions and replicates.

## Repository layout

| Folder | Contents |
|----|----|
| `R/` | Package source — 100+ exported functions (loaders, annotation, counting, statistics, plotting, export) plus the [`run_howmahico_report()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/run_howmahico_report.md)/[`derive_filtered_annotation()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/derive_filtered_annotation.md) entry points |
| `inst/rmarkdown/templates/` | The parameterized Rmd report templates — `00_mhc_report` (all-in-one), `00_mhc_upsets`, and the focused `01_id_counts`/`02_overlaps`/`03_lcms_qc`/`04_quant`/`05_quality_score`/`06_quant_stats`/`07_pepchem`/`08_prot_all` — packaged for [`rmarkdown::draft()`](https://pkgs.rstudio.com/rmarkdown/reference/draft.html)/[`run_howmahico_report()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/run_howmahico_report.md). Shared setup for the focused reports lives in `inst/rmarkdown/shared/setup.Rmd` |
| `inst/scripts/` | The guided pipeline script handed out by [`get_pipeline_script()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/get_pipeline_script.md) |
| `vignettes/` | [`vignette("howmahico")`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/articles/howmahico.md) — the narrated walkthrough |
| `tests/testthat/` | testthat-edition-3 suite (hand-synthesized fixtures — never derived from real instrument data) |
| `man/` | Generated roxygen2 documentation (`.Rd`) |
| `example/` | Legacy pre-package reference copies — gitignored, for reference only |

The numbered folders `1_documentation/`, `2_data/`, `3_results/`,
`4_figures/` are the **convention for your own analysis project**, not
part of this repository — they are what the `Folder*` parameters point
at by default. Create them wherever you keep the data; the package does
not care where they live, and any absolute path works.

## Requirements

- **R \>= 4.1.0** (the package uses the native `|>` pipe)
- **pandoc**, to render the HTML reports. Bundled with
  [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/); install it
  separately if you work outside RStudio. RStudio itself is optional
  (the repo does ship an `HowMaHiCo.Rproj` if you use it)
- All dependencies are declared in `DESCRIPTION` and resolved
  automatically — no manual library list, no companion-package install
- **Optional:** [limma](https://bioconductor.org/packages/limma) for the
  advanced-quantification report (`BiocManager::install("limma")`).
  Without it that report falls back to a Welch t-test automatically

## How to run

**1. Install the package**

``` r

# from a local clone:
devtools::load_all()
# or from GitHub:
devtools::install_github("DavidGZ1/HowMaHiCo")
library(HowMaHiCo)
```

**2. Auto-generate an annotation CSV skeleton**

``` r

# FragPipe (psm.tsv layout)
get_annot_fragpipe(dir_data = "2_data") |>
  write.csv(row.names = FALSE, file = "1_documentation/sample_annotation.csv")

# DIA-NN (report.tsv layout)
get_annot_diann(dir_data = "2_data") |>
  write.csv(row.names = FALSE, file = "1_documentation/sample_annotation_diann.csv")

# PEAKS (export folders)
get_annot_peaks(dir_data = "2_data/peaks_export") |>
  write.csv(row.names = FALSE, file = "1_documentation/sample_annotation_peaks.csv")
```

These scan `2_data` and write one row per data file — no
`sample_list.xlsx` needed to get started (`Sample_ID` can be filled in
next, by hand or optionally from a HyStar sample list).

**3. Complete the annotation CSV**

Open the generated CSV and fill in the experimental metadata:
`Condition`, `BioReplicate`, `TechReplicate`, `Sample_ID`. Verify that
`Sample_folder` matches the data subfolder names exactly, then save. The
column is the same for every search engine; tables from older runs that
use the engine-specific `Sample_fp` (FragPipe/DIA-NN) or `Sample_peaks`
(PEAKS) still load unchanged.

> **Two things the annotation table controls:** - **Inclusion** — only
> samples listed in the annotation table are read and reported. Any
> sample present in the results folder but missing from the table is
> silently excluded, so the table is also how you subset a run. -
> **Ordering** — Conditions, replicates and samples appear in every plot
> and table in the **row order of the annotation CSV**. Order the rows
> the way you want them displayed (factor levels are taken from first
> appearance).

*(Optional)* `Sample_ID` can be populated automatically from a Bruker
HyStar sample list with
[`get_annot_sampleid()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/get_annot_sampleid.md)
instead of typing it by hand:

``` r

read.csv("1_documentation/sample_annotation.csv") |>
  get_annot_sampleid(file_sample_list = "1_documentation/sample_list.xlsx") |>
  write.csv(row.names = FALSE, file = "1_documentation/sample_annotation.csv")
```

[`get_annot_sampleid()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/get_annot_sampleid.md)
joins on `Source_file`, so both sides must use the same run naming. It
warns when nothing matched (showing example values from each side) and
when only some rows matched (naming the dropped ones); pass
`keep_all = TRUE` to keep every annotation row instead, with the
unmatched `Sample_ID` left empty.

**4. (Optional) Get a local copy of the report template to customise**

``` r

get_report_template("MyReport", template = "00_mhc_report")
```

**5. Render a report**

**Edit these for your run** (the rest can stay at the example defaults):

- `SampleSet` / `Subset` — experiment name and subset label (used in the
  title, filenames, and output subfolders)
- `FolderDocumentation` / `FolderData` / `FolderResults` /
  `FolderFigures` — absolute (or render-time-cwd-relative) paths
- `AnnotationFile` — the CSV filled in above
- `Software` — `fragpipe_dda_combined` \| `fragpipe_dda_individual` \|
  `diann` \| `peaks_xpro` \| `custom`
- `Instrument` — `tims_tof` \| `faims_orbi` \| `orbi`
- `MHCclass` — `MHC1` (human, 8–13 AA), `MHC1_mouse` (murine H-2, 7–11
  AA) or `MHC2` (12–25 AA)
- `Provider` — your lab or platform, printed in the report header; leave
  empty for a generic attribution
- `output_file` — the HTML filename to write

The full parameter reference is in the [Parameters](#parameters) section
below.

``` r

run_howmahico_report(
  template = "00_mhc_report",          # or "00_mhc_upsets"
  params = list(
    SampleSet        = "project_id",
    Provider         = "My Lab",      # "" prints a generic attribution
    DataAnalysisNames = "analyst",
    WetLabNames      = "operator",
    FolderDocumentation = "1_documentation",
    AnnotationFile   = "sample_annotation.csv",
    Subset           = "dda_all",
    FolderData       = "2_data",
    FolderResults    = "3_results",
    FolderFigures    = "4_figures",
    # ProjectDir     = getwd(),   # set if rendering from a subdirectory
    Instrument       = "tims_tof",    # faims_orbi | orbi
    Software         = "fragpipe_dda_combined",
    MHCclass         = "MHC1",        # MHC1 (8-13 AA) | MHC1_mouse (7-11 AA) | MHC2 (12-25 AA)
    TestMode         = FALSE,
    ResultsOverwrite = TRUE,
    PlotsSave        = FALSE,
    CsvSave          = FALSE
  ),
  output_file = "01_report_main__hla1_dda_all.html"
)
```

`FolderDocumentation`/`FolderData`/`FolderResults`/`FolderFigures` are
absolute (or render-time-working-directory-relative) paths — the
template ships inside an installed package and can be rendered from
anywhere. One call renders one report; loop with
[`derive_filtered_annotation()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/derive_filtered_annotation.md)
for multi-subset batch runs (see the `\dontrun{}` example on
`run_howmahico_report`).

**Focused reports (instead of the all-in-one `00_mhc_report`)** — build
the `pep_all` cache once with
[`build_pep_all()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/build_pep_all.md),
then render any subset of the smaller, purpose-focused templates against
it (no re-parsing per report):

``` r

annot <- read_annot("1_documentation/sample_annotation.csv")
build_pep_all(software = "fragpipe_dda_combined", folder_data = "2_data",
              annotation = annot, shortpep_range = c(8, 13),
              file_rda = "2_data/dda_all_pep_all.rda")

for (tmpl in c("01_id_counts",     # ID counts, size distributions, motifs, PTM
               "02_overlaps",      # replicate / condition / pairwise overlap
               "03_lcms_qc",       # RT/1k0/mz, Score/ppm (advanced)
               "04_quant",         # log2(Area) correlation, Area %CV
               "05_quality_score", # per-sample immunopeptidomics quality score
               "06_quant_stats",   # differential abundance between Conditions
               "07_pepchem",       # amino-acid composition, motifs, GRAVY & co.
               "08_prot_all")) {   # source proteins, ligands per protein
  run_howmahico_report(tmpl,
                       params = list(SampleSet = "project_id", Subset = "dda_all",
                                     FolderData = "2_data", FolderResults = "3_results",
                                     FolderFigures = "4_figures",
                                     Software = "fragpipe_dda_combined"),
                       output_file = paste0(tmpl, "__dda_all.html"))
}
```

Each focused report chooses how to obtain `pep_all` via the
`PepAllSource` param: `"cached"` (default — load the
`<Subset>_pep_all.rda` cache), `"rda"` (load an explicit `PepAllFile`),
or `"build"` (parse the raw search output itself, no separate
[`build_pep_all()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/build_pep_all.md)
call). So to render a single focused report directly from results, pass
`PepAllSource = "build"` (plus `Software`, `AnnotationFile`,
`FolderDocumentation`) and skip the
[`build_pep_all()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/build_pep_all.md)
step above.

`00_mhc_report` (all-in-one) and `00_mhc_upsets` are unchanged and still
parse the raw files themselves.

`06_quant_stats` compares peptide `Area` between Conditions
(normalization, data completeness, PCA and clustered/unclustered
heatmaps, then per-pair differential abundance with volcano plots and a
presence/absence track for condition-exclusive ligands). It uses
[limma](https://bioconductor.org/packages/limma), an optional
Bioconductor dependency — install it with
`BiocManager::install("limma")`, or render with `StatMethod = "ttest"`
(and `NormMethod = "median"`) for a Bioconductor-free run; the report
falls back to that automatically when limma is missing. Its methods and
their justification are documented in the report itself.

Reports are written to `output_file` (HTML), and result tables/figures
are written under `<FolderResults>/<subset>/` and
`<FolderFigures>/<subset>/`.

## The reports

| Template | What it gives you | Needs |
|----|----|----|
| `00_mhc_report` | All-in-one QC report: ID counts, overlaps, size/charge distributions, RT–ion-mobility–*m/z* distributions, Area correlation and %CV, Score/ppm QC, motifs, PTM profile | raw files (parses them itself) |
| `00_mhc_upsets` | Overlap / UpSet plots only | `pep_all` cache |
| `01_id_counts` | Identification counts (mean ± sd per Condition / BioReplicate / Sample), length and charge distributions, sequence motifs, PTM profile | cache |
| `02_overlaps` | Intra-Condition replicate overlap (counts and %), cross-Condition UpSet, pairwise overlap matrices | cache |
| `03_lcms_qc` | RT / ion-mobility / *m/z* distributions, pseudochromatograms and pseudomobilograms, Score and mass-error QC | cache |
| `04_quant` | log2(Area) Pearson correlation between samples, Area %CV violins | cache |
| `05_quality_score` | Per-sample immunopeptidomics quality score (0–100) with a traffic-light overview and per-metric breakdown | cache |
| `06_quant_stats` | Differential abundance between Conditions: normalization, completeness, PCA, heatmaps, volcano/MA, plus a presence/absence track for condition-exclusive ligands | cache; limma optional |
| `07_pepchem` | Amino-acid composition, per-position residue frequency, and descriptors (GRAVY, pI, charge, …) compared between Conditions | cache |
| `08_prot_all` | Protein level: source proteins per sample, ligands per protein, top source proteins, detection breadth, and any protein-level values the search engine reported | cache |

The seven focused reports each render one slice of the analysis and are
independent — render only the ones you need. `00_mhc_report` covers most
of `01`–`04` in a single document.

## Parameters

Every template accepts the common set; each report adds its own. All
parameters are written to `<report>_input_params.csv` on every run, so a
report always records how it was produced.

### Common to every report

| Param | Purpose |
|----|----|
| `SampleSet` | Experiment name, used in the auto-generated report title |
| `Provider` | Organisation/person that produced the report, printed in the header. Empty (default) prints a generic attribution |
| `Subset` | Subset label — becomes a filename prefix and a subfolder under `FolderResults`/`FolderFigures` |
| `DataAnalysisNames` / `WetLabNames` | Free-text credits shown in the header |
| `FolderDocumentation` | Folder containing `AnnotationFile` |
| `AnnotationFile` | Annotation CSV name within `FolderDocumentation` |
| `FolderData` | Raw search output, and where the `pep_all` cache is read/written |
| `FolderResults` / `FolderFigures` | csv+xlsx output / png output |
| `ProjectDir` | Project root; relative folder paths resolve from here. Set it when rendering from a subdirectory |
| `Software` | `fragpipe_dda_combined` \| `fragpipe_dda_individual` \| `diann` \| `peaks_xpro` \| `custom` — selects the loader |
| `Instrument` | `tims_tof` \| `faims_orbi` \| `orbi` — only affects PEAKS ion-mobility parsing |
| `MHCclass` | `MHC1` (human, 8–13 AA) \| `MHC1_mouse` (murine H-2, 7–11 AA) \| `MHC2` (12–25 AA). Overrides `ShortPeptideLength*` |
| `ShortPeptideLengthMin` / `Max` | Custom length window, used only when `MHCclass` is not one of the three above |
| `TestMode` | `TRUE` keeps ~100 rows **per run** — a fast dry run that preserves every run/Condition/replicate |
| `ResultsOverwrite` | `FALSE` aborts rather than overwriting results from an earlier run |
| `CsvSave` / `PlotsSave` | Also write the intermediate csv tables / every figure as png |

Folder paths are absolute, or relative to the working directory you
render from — the templates live inside the installed package and can be
rendered from anywhere.

### Focused reports only

| Param | Purpose |
|----|----|
| `PepAllSource` | How to obtain `pep_all`: `"cached"` (default — load `<Subset>_pep_all.rda`), `"rda"` (load `PepAllFile`), or `"build"` (parse the raw output itself, skipping [`build_pep_all()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/build_pep_all.md)) |
| `PepAllFile` | Explicit `.rda` path, used only with `PepAllSource = "rda"` |

### `05_quality_score`

| Param | Purpose |
|----|----|
| `QCColumn` | Annotation column flagging QC control samples (default `"QC"`; empty disables) |
| `ThresholdMode` | `"default"` (literature thresholds) or `"qc_relative"` (calibrate from the QC samples) |

### `06_quant_stats`

| Param | Purpose |
|----|----|
| `PeptideSet` | `"selected"` (the MHC length window) or `"all"` |
| `QuantFeature` / `QuantUnit` | Matrix rows (`Peptide` \| `Sequence` \| `PeptideID` \| `ProteinFirst`) and columns (`BioReplicate` \| `Sample` \| `Condition`) |
| `MinReplicates` | A feature is tested when quantified in ≥ this many units of ≥ 1 Condition |
| `NormMethod` | `median` \| `quantile` \| `cyclicloess` \| `scale` \| `none` |
| `ImputeMethod` | `none` \| `minprob` \| `mindet` |
| `StatMethod` | `limma` (moderated t) or `ttest` (Welch — no Bioconductor dependency) |
| `BlockVar` | Optional column for [`limma::duplicateCorrelation`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/limma/man/dupcor.html) |
| `FdrCutoff` / `Log2FcCutoff` | Significance cut-offs |
| `MinDetectExclusive` | Detection count required to call a feature condition-exclusive |
| `TopNHeatmap` / `PermutationTest` | Heatmap feature count; whether to run the PERMANOVA test |

### `07_pepchem`

| Param | Purpose |
|----|----|
| `PeptideSet` | `"selected"` or `"all"` |
| `PropertySet` | `core` (Length, GRAVY, pI, Charge) or `extended` (+ MW, Boman, hydrophobic moment, instability/aliphatic index, AA class fractions) |
| `MotifLength` | Length used for the per-position frequency map: `"auto"` (modal) or an integer |
| `TerminalPositions` | Comma-separated positions profiled across all lengths; negative counts from the C-terminus |
| `ChargePh` | pH for the net-charge descriptor |
| `MinPeptidesSample` | Samples with fewer unique sequences are flagged as unreliable |
| `FdrCutoff` | BH significance cut-off |

## Output

Written on **every** run, to `<FolderResults>/<Subset>/`:

| File | Contents |
|----|----|
| `<Subset>_pep_all.csv` | The unified peptide table |
| `<Subset>_counts_pep_all_condition.csv` | Identification counts per Condition |
| `<Subset>_seq_by_condition.xlsx` | Peptide sequences per Condition |
| `<Subset>_<report>_input_params.csv` | Every parameter used, plus package version and timestamp |

Plus each report’s own result tables (`quant_stats_results.csv`,
`pepchem_summary.csv`, …). `CsvSave = TRUE` adds the intermediate tables
(per-sample log2Area matrices, count summaries, upset tables);
`PlotsSave = TRUE` writes every figure as png to
`<FolderFigures>/<Subset>/`. The HTML report itself goes to
`output_file`.

[`build_pep_all()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/build_pep_all.md)
also writes the `<Subset>_pep_all.rda` cache into `FolderData`, which is
what the focused reports read.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|----|----|
| `render params not declared in YAML: X` | The template has no parameter `X`. Check the tables above — report-specific params only exist on their own report |
| `pep_all cache not found at ...` | No [`build_pep_all()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/build_pep_all.md) run yet for this `Subset`. Either run it, or render with `PepAllSource = "build"` |
| `The following result files were found and they cannot be overwritten` | Results from an earlier run are in the way. Move them, or set `ResultsOverwrite = TRUE` |
| `Files listed in the annotation table were not found` | `FolderData` or the `Sample_folder` column does not match the data layout |
| A sample is missing from the report | It is not listed in the annotation table — only listed samples are read |
| `This step needs the 'limma' package` | `BiocManager::install("limma")`, or render `06_quant_stats` with `StatMethod = "ttest"` and `NormMethod = "median"` |
| Only one Condition, and comparison sections are empty | Expected — pairwise sections need ≥ 2 Conditions and say so rather than failing |
| Plots or correlations look wrong after a quick run | `TestMode = TRUE` keeps ~100 rows per run; correlations need the full data |
| `pandoc` errors when rendering | pandoc is missing or not on `PATH`. Use RStudio, or install pandoc separately |

# Package index

## Render reports

Entry points that build the cached pep_all table and render the
parameterized QC report templates (00_mhc_report all-in-one, or the
focused 01-07 reports)

- [`build_pep_all()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/build_pep_all.md)
  :

  Build (and optionally cache) the unified `pep_all` table from raw
  search output

- [`run_howmahico_report()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/run_howmahico_report.md)
  : Render a HowMaHiCo QC report from the installed package templates

- [`derive_filtered_annotation()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/derive_filtered_annotation.md)
  : Derive a Condition-filtered copy of a sample annotation file

- [`get_report_template()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/get_report_template.md)
  : Get the HowMaHiCo templates

- [`get_pipeline_script()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/get_pipeline_script.md)
  : Copy the guided analysis-pipeline script to the working directory

## Annotation

Read, validate, display, and auto-generate sample annotation tables

- [`read_annot()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/read_annot.md)
  : Read, validate, and reformat a sample annotation table
- [`print_annot()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/print_annot.md)
  : Render an annotation table as an interactive HTML datatable
- [`get_annot_fragpipe()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/get_annot_fragpipe.md)
  : Auto-generate a skeleton annotation table from FragPipe psm.tsv
  files
- [`get_annot_diann()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/get_annot_diann.md)
  : Auto-generate a skeleton annotation table from DIA-NN report.tsv
  files
- [`get_annot_peaks()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/get_annot_peaks.md)
  : Auto-generate a skeleton annotation table from a PEAKS export folder
- [`get_annot_sampleid()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/get_annot_sampleid.md)
  : Enrich an annotation table with Sample_ID from a Bruker HyStar
  sample list

## Report helpers

Shared settings the report templates derive from their params: the MHC
length window and palette, and the Condition pairs to compare

- [`mhc_length_window()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/mhc_length_window.md)
  : Peptide-length window of an MHC class
- [`mhc_class_palette()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/mhc_class_palette.md)
  : Two-colour fill palette of an MHC class
- [`mhc_classes()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/mhc_classes.md)
  : Names of the built-in MHC classes
- [`condition_pairs()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/condition_pairs.md)
  : All pairwise Condition comparisons
- [`provider_line()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/provider_line.md)
  : Provider sentence of a report header

## Data loaders

Software-specific loader families that converge on the unified `pep_all`
schema

- [`read_fragpipe()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/read_fragpipe.md)
  :

  Read one FragPipe `psm.tsv` or DIA-NN `report.tsv` file

- [`read_fragpipe_batch()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/read_fragpipe_batch.md)
  :

  Batch-read FragPipe `psm.tsv` files and merge them

- [`parse_fragpipe()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/parse_fragpipe.md)
  :

  Parse raw FragPipe PSM results into `pep_all` format

- [`annotate_fragpipe()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/annotate_fragpipe.md)
  : Join parsed FragPipe results to the sample annotation table

- [`read_diann()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/read_diann.md)
  :

  Read one DIA-NN `report.tsv` file

- [`read_diann_batch()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/read_diann_batch.md)
  :

  Batch-read DIA-NN `report.tsv` files and merge them

- [`parse_diann()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/parse_diann.md)
  :

  Parse raw DIA-NN report results into `pep_all` format

- [`annotate_diann()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/annotate_diann.md)
  : Join parsed DIA-NN results to the sample annotation table

- [`read_peaks()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/read_peaks.md)
  :

  Read one PEAKS `peptide.csv` export into long format

- [`read_peaks_batch()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/read_peaks_batch.md)
  : Batch-read PEAKS export folders and merge them into raw long format

- [`parse_peaks()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/parse_peaks.md)
  :

  Parse raw PEAKS results into `pep_all` format

- [`annotate_peaks()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/annotate_peaks.md)
  : Join parsed PEAKS results to the sample annotation table

## Custom (dictionary-driven) parsing

The `software = "custom"` path: ingest a tabular export from a tool with
no built-in loader by editing a YAML dictionary instead of writing R
code.

- [`get_dictionary_template()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/get_dictionary_template.md)
  : Copy the custom-parser dictionary template to the working directory

- [`read_dictionary()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/read_dictionary.md)
  : Read and validate a HowMaHiCo parser dictionary

- [`read_custom_batch()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/read_custom_batch.md)
  : Batch-read a generic per-sample tabular export

- [`parse_unified()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/parse_unified.md)
  :

  Parse a raw search-engine export into `pep_all` via a dictionary

- [`annotate_unified()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/annotate_unified.md)
  : Join a dictionary-parsed table to the sample annotation

## Checks

Guard against clobbering existing output and summarise global ID
composition

- [`check_file_exists()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/check_file_exists.md)
  : Check whether a single output file already exists
- [`check_output_exists()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/check_output_exists.md)
  : Check whether any of the report's standard output files already
  exist
- [`check_ids_global()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/check_ids_global.md)
  : Total ID counts split by protein/decoy/contaminant assignment

## Counting & overlap analysis

Tabulate ID counts, charge/area summaries, sequence lists, and
cross-condition overlaps

- [`count_ids()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/count_ids.md)
  : Count distinct peptides, sequences, and proteins

- [`count_ids_condition_bylengthrange()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/count_ids_condition_bylengthrange.md)
  :

  ID counts and proportions by `Length_range` and `Condition`

- [`count_ids_by()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/count_ids_by.md)
  : Wide table of peptide identifications by an arbitrary grouping

- [`get_charge_group()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/get_charge_group.md)
  :

  Classify charge states into `+1`/`+2`/`>= +3` groups

- [`get_proportion_charge()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/get_proportion_charge.md)
  : Proportions of each charge group within a count table

- [`get_mat_log2area()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/get_mat_log2area.md)
  :

  Build a `Log2Area` matrix for clustering/heatmaps/correlation

- [`summarise_area()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/summarise_area.md)
  : Per-peptide Area mean/sd/%CV summary by group

- [`list_sequences()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/list_sequences.md)
  : List unique peptide sequences per group

- [`count_intersect()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/count_intersect.md)
  : Count distinct elements shared between two conditions

- [`count_merged()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/count_merged.md)
  : Count distinct elements across the union of two conditions

- [`count_samples_patients()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/count_samples_patients.md)
  : Combined per-Patient/Sample_type/Condition sample-and-patient count
  summary

- [`select_unique()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/select_unique.md)
  : Select distinct rows on a subset of columns

- [`filter_unique()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/filter_unique.md)
  : Filter rows and drop to distinct/unused-level state

## Plotting

QC plots covering ID size/charge distributions, overlaps, motifs, and
correlation

- [`plot_peplength_dens()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_peplength_dens.md)
  : Peptide length distribution: boxplot + density histogram

- [`plot_peplength_hist()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_peplength_hist.md)
  : Peptide length histogram faceted by Condition

- [`plot_pepmass()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_pepmass.md)
  : Peptide mass distribution: boxplot + density histogram with apex
  annotation

- [`plot_pepmz()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_pepmz.md)
  : Peptide m/z distribution: boxplot + density histogram with apex
  annotation

- [`plot_bp_count_length()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_bp_count_length.md)
  : Stacked bar chart of total ID counts per Condition, split by length
  range

- [`plot_count_mean_sd()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_count_mean_sd.md)
  : Mean ± SD barplot of ID counts per Condition, faceted by length
  range

- [`plot_prop_length_condition()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_prop_length_condition.md)
  :

  Stacked bar chart of peptide proportions by `Length_range` and
  `Condition`

- [`plot_charge_proportions()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_charge_proportions.md)
  : Stacked bar chart of charge-state proportions by group

- [`plot_overlap_intra_condition()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_overlap_intra_condition.md)
  : Overlap barplot for one ID level

- [`plot_upset()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_upset.md)
  : UpSet plot of overlap between groups for a given variable

- [`plot_upset_batch()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_upset_batch.md)
  : Batch of UpSet plots across several variables

- [`plot_pseudochromatogram()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_pseudochromatogram.md)
  : Peptide ID pseudochromatogram: count vs RT, faceted by Condition

- [`plot_pseudomobilogram()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_pseudomobilogram.md)
  : Peptide ID pseudomobilogram: count vs 1/k0, faceted by Condition

- [`plot_2d_distribution()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_2d_distribution.md)
  : 2D binned heatmap for any two continuous peptide properties

- [`plot_violin_areacv()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_violin_areacv.md)
  : Violin + boxplot of Area %CV by group

- [`plot_qc_box()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_qc_box.md)
  : Boxplot of Score or mass error per Condition and charge

- [`plot_qc_violin()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_qc_violin.md)
  : Violin + overlaid boxplot of Score or mass error per Condition and
  charge

- [`plot_corr()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_corr.md)
  : Pearson correlation heatmap of log2(Area)

- [`plot_ptm_heatmap()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_ptm_heatmap.md)
  : Heatmap of PTM counts or proportions for length-filtered peptides

- [`ggseqlogo_bylength()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/ggseqlogo_bylength.md)
  : Sequence motif logo for peptides of a given length

- [`theme_rawr()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/theme_rawr.md)
  : HowMaHiCo's shared ggplot theme

- [`theme_howmahico()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/theme_howmahico.md)
  : HowMaHiCo's unified ggplot theme

## Sample quality score

Per-sample immunopeptidomics quality score behind the 05_quality_score
report: raw signals (length-window fidelity, canonical-length dominance,
anchor-motif clarity, non-tryptic specificity, charge plausibility,
depth, mass accuracy, cross-class contamination), the threshold model,
and the weighted 0-100 composite.

- [`score_sample_quality()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/score_sample_quality.md)
  : Score immunopeptidomics samples for overall quality
- [`qc_metrics_by_sample()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/qc_metrics_by_sample.md)
  : Raw per-sample immunopeptidomics quality metrics
- [`anchor_information_content()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/anchor_information_content.md)
  : Per-position anchor information content of equal-length peptides
- [`score_curve()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/score_curve.md)
  : Map a raw metric value to a 0-100 quality sub-score
- [`quality_thresholds_default()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/quality_thresholds_default.md)
  : Default quality-score thresholds and weights
- [`calibrate_thresholds_from_qc()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/calibrate_thresholds_from_qc.md)
  : Derive QC-relative thresholds from tagged quality-control samples
- [`plot_quality_heatmap()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_quality_heatmap.md)
  : Traffic-light heatmap of per-sample quality sub-scores
- [`plot_quality_composite()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_quality_composite.md)
  : Per-sample composite quality-score bar chart
- [`plot_cross_class_length()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_cross_class_length.md)
  : Per-sample peptide-length histogram highlighting cross-class
  contamination

## Advanced quantification & statistics

Build the quantitative matrix and compare peptide Area between
Conditions (filtering, normalization, imputation, limma moderated t /
Welch t, Fisher presence-absence, PERMANOVA) plus the plots of the
06_quant_stats report

- [`build_quant_matrix()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/build_quant_matrix.md)
  :

  Build a feature x unit log2(Area) matrix from `pep_all`

- [`filter_quant()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/filter_quant.md)
  : Filter a quantitative matrix to testable features

- [`normalize_quant()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/normalize_quant.md)
  : Between-sample normalization of a log2 intensity matrix

- [`impute_quant()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/impute_quant.md)
  : Left-censored imputation of missing quantitative values

- [`test_differential()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/test_differential.md)
  : Differential abundance between conditions

- [`test_detection()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/test_detection.md)
  : Presence/absence test between conditions (Fisher exact)

- [`combine_quant_results()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/combine_quant_results.md)
  : Combine the quantitative and presence/absence tracks

- [`summarise_significant()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/summarise_significant.md)
  : Count significant features per contrast

- [`permanova_condition()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/permanova_condition.md)
  : Global permutation test of condition separation (PERMANOVA)

- [`plot_completeness()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_completeness.md)
  : Data completeness of a quantitative matrix

- [`plot_missing_heatmap()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_missing_heatmap.md)
  : Presence/absence map of a quantitative matrix

- [`plot_intensity_dist()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_intensity_dist.md)
  : Intensity distribution per unit (normalization diagnostic)

- [`plot_dynamic_range()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_dynamic_range.md)
  : Dynamic range (rank-abundance) per condition

- [`plot_pca()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_pca.md)
  : Principal component analysis of a quantitative matrix

- [`plot_quant_heatmap()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_quant_heatmap.md)
  : Heatmap of a quantitative matrix, clustered or in annotation order

- [`plot_volcano()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_volcano.md)
  : Volcano plot of a differential-abundance result

- [`plot_ma()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_ma.md)
  : MA plot of a differential-abundance result

- [`plot_pvalue_hist()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_pvalue_hist.md)
  : P-value histogram (test calibration diagnostic)

- [`plot_sig_summary()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_sig_summary.md)
  : Significant-feature counts per contrast

## Physicochemical properties

Peptide-chemistry engine behind the 07_pepchem report: amino-acid
composition, per-position residue frequency and per-peptide descriptors
(GRAVY, pI, charge, …), summarised per sample and compared between
Conditions.

- [`peptide_properties()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/peptide_properties.md)
  : Per-sequence physicochemical descriptors
- [`pepchem_properties()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/pepchem_properties.md)
  : Descriptor columns of a property set
- [`aa_composition()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/aa_composition.md)
  : Position-independent amino-acid composition
- [`aa_position_frequency()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/aa_position_frequency.md)
  : Per-position amino-acid frequency
- [`pepchem_by_sample()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/pepchem_by_sample.md)
  : Per-sample peptide physicochemical descriptors
- [`summarise_pepchem()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/summarise_pepchem.md)
  : Summarise peptide descriptors within a group
- [`aggregate_pepchem()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/aggregate_pepchem.md)
  : Aggregate per-sample descriptor summaries to Conditions
- [`cliffs_delta()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/cliffs_delta.md)
  : Cliff's delta effect size
- [`compare_pepchem()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/compare_pepchem.md)
  : Compare peptide descriptors between Conditions
- [`compare_aa_frequency()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/compare_aa_frequency.md)
  : Compare amino-acid frequencies between Conditions
- [`plot_aa_composition()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_aa_composition.md)
  : Amino-acid composition across groups
- [`plot_aa_position_heatmap()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_aa_position_heatmap.md)
  : Per-position amino-acid frequency heatmap
- [`plot_property_distribution()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_property_distribution.md)
  : Distribution of one peptide descriptor across Conditions
- [`plot_property_sample_summary()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_property_sample_summary.md)
  : Per-Condition mean +/- sd of a descriptor across samples
- [`plot_property_effectsize()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_property_effectsize.md)
  : Effect sizes of the between-condition comparison

## Protein-level analysis

Condenses the peptide table to source-protein level (the `prot_all`
table behind the 08_prot_all report), including the protein-level values
the search engine itself reported.

- [`build_prot_all()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/build_prot_all.md)
  :

  Condense `pep_all` to one row per protein and sample

- [`summarise_prot_all()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/summarise_prot_all.md)
  : Condense the protein table across samples

- [`top_source_proteins()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/top_source_proteins.md)
  : Rank the most prolific source proteins

- [`expand_mapped_proteins()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/expand_mapped_proteins.md)
  : Expand peptides onto every protein they map to

- [`prot_engine_columns()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/prot_engine_columns.md)
  : Protein-level columns the search engine reported

- [`diann_protein_columns()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/diann_protein_columns.md)
  : Engine-reported protein-level column names

- [`plot_proteins_per_sample()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_proteins_per_sample.md)
  : Source proteins identified per sample

- [`plot_peptides_per_protein()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_peptides_per_protein.md)
  : Distribution of ligands per source protein

- [`plot_top_proteins()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_top_proteins.md)
  : Ranked bar chart of the most prolific source proteins

- [`plot_protein_detection()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_protein_detection.md)
  : How widely each source protein is detected

- [`plot_ligand_vs_protein_quant()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/plot_ligand_vs_protein_quant.md)
  : Summed ligand intensity against the search engine's protein quantity

## Export & I/O helpers

Write report outputs (plots, csvs, render parameters) to disk

- [`ggsave_rawr()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/ggsave_rawr.md)
  : Save a ggplot to a folder, skipping plots that were never built
- [`ggprint_rawr()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/ggprint_rawr.md)
  : Print a plot, skipping ones that were never built
- [`write.csv_rawr()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/write.csv_rawr.md)
  : Write a data frame to csv, named after the variable that was passed
  in
- [`write_input_params()`](https://davidgz1.github.io/HowMaHiCo/reference/write_input_params.md)
  : Write a report's render parameters to csv
